provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: The rule is already the same in all four directions. Each non-background, non-anchor single-colour object (4-connected) that is orthogonally adjacent to an anchor cell slides straight away from that anchor until it reaches the grid border. D4 transforms only permute the four push directions. Because the emitted program detects the direction from the visible adjacency in the actual grid coordinates, no reorientation is needed. Palette roles are fixed as constants: background = palette[7] and anchor = palette[9]. All movers are found from the input, all of them are erased, and then each one slides until it would leave the grid or hit a non-background cell. Erasing first makes the result independent of processing order. Distractors and anchors stay where they are. Objects already on the border have k=0 and stay put.
draft_notes.limitations: Not run or tested. The program assumes the constructor's guarantees: each mover touches anchors from exactly one side, every non-anchor object has a unique colour, and slide paths are clear. If an object touched anchors from several sides, the first side found in scan order would be used, which is ambiguous. The stop-at-obstacle check is only a safeguard; the generator never needs it. The fixtures are consistent with the uniform rule.
